title: Within‐person relations between mobile phone addiction and mental well‐being among college students: The moderating role of negative self‐schema
abstract: Abstract Mobile phone addiction has been linked to poorer mental well‐being, yet the direction of this relationship at the within‐person level remains unclear. A three‐wave longitudinal study followed 1462 college students (M age = 18.60, SD age = 0.83). Mobile phone addiction, negative self‐schema, and mental well‐being were assessed at each wave, and a random intercept cross‐lagged panel model (RI‐CLPM) was used to separate within‐person dynamics from between‐person differences. Negative self‐schema was assessed at each wave, and its between‐person component was used as the moderator. At the within‐person level, we found that higher‐than‐usual mobile phone addiction was associated with subsequent decreases in mental well‐being ( β T1→T2 = −0.09, p < 0.01; β T2→T3 = −0.09, p < 0.05), whereas the reverse path was not significant. In addition, negative self‐schema moderated this association. Specifically, among individuals with higher levels of negative self‐schema, greater mobile phone addiction was associated with lower subsequent mental well‐being ( β = −0.134, p < 0.01), whereas this effect was not significant among individuals with lower levels of negative self‐schema ( β = 0.003, p > 0.05). These findings highlight negative self‐schema as an important vulnerability factor linking mobile phone addiction to poorer mental well‐being and may inform intervention efforts.
